newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen says steel merger best solution.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen says steel merger best solution.

text.p: A merger of steel operations between Thyssen and Krupp offers better prospects for workers than a hostile takeover by Krupp would have done, Thyssen AG Chief Executive Dieter Vogel said on Tuesday.

"What would have happened under a hostile takeover would have been far worse than what will happen now that Thyssen will steer the fusion," Vogel told WDR television after Fried. Krupp Hoesch-Krupp withdrew its cash bid on Monday.
Vogel added that now the threat of a wholesale takeover was gone, the two companies could work out the details of steel cooperation intensively and soberly.

Despite the abandonment of Krupp's takeover gambit, 30,000 steel workers demonstrated in Germany's financial capital Frankfurt on Tuesday to protest against the power of the banks behind the bid and job losses they still expect to hit them.
Vogel said that financing an all-out takeover bid would have forced Krupp to raise a massive 15 billion marks ($8.9 billion) in debt.
"The workers would have borne the brunt," Vogel said, adding such a manoeuvre would push the limits of what was socially acceptable.
Both sides said on Monday talks were going well on forming the steel venture, which would be controlled by Thyssen, whose steel operations are bigger and more profitable.

Around 6,000 steel workers at Krupp's Dortmund works stayed away from work on Tuesday, demanding written guarantees that there would be no more job losses over and above the 2,200 announced earlier this year under a cost-cutting plan.
The steel workers fear that they may face most job losses, because Krupp's plants are less modern than Thyssen's.
